title: AG-UI Overview - Agent User Interaction Protocol
snippet: AG-UI (Agent–User Interaction Protocol) is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how agents connect to user-facing applications. Developed by CopilotKit and released in early 2025, AG-UI is an open protocol for bidirectional, event-driven communication between AI agents and frontend applications.
claim: AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol for bidirectional agent-to-UI communication released in early 2025.

topic: AG-UI event stream types for human approval and state updates
query: agent human interaction streaming typed events approval interface
title: AG-UI: How the Agent-User Interaction Protocol Works | Codecademy
snippet: AG-UI supports around 16 event types across five categories: Lifecycle (starting/finishing runs), Text Messages (streaming text), Tool Calls (executing functions), State Management (syncing data), and Special events (pausing for approval or custom needs).
claim: AG-UI defines 16 standardized event types across 5 categories including lifecycle, messages, tool calls, state, and approval events.

topic: AG-UI human approval interrupt model for agent control
query: agent human interaction streaming typed events approval interface
title: AG-UI Integration with Agent Framework | Microsoft Learn
snippet: AG-UI's interrupt model lets agents pause execution, request human approval, accept modifications, and resume safely. An agent can pause mid-execution and ask for approval (like "I'm about to delete these 47 records. Do you want to proceed?"), and the user can click approve or cancel, allowing the agent to either continue or backtrack without the session ending.
claim: AG-UI enables agents to pause, request approval, and resume based on human decision without session termination.

topic: A2A task state machine for human input and approval workflows
query: A2A input-required task state human approval workflow
title: Life of a Task - A2A Protocol
snippet: Tasks have lifecycle states such as submitted, working, input-required, or completed. A2A v1.0 defines a full Task state machine with nine named states: TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED, TASK_STATE_WORKING, TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED, TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED, TASK_STATE_COMPLETED, TASK_STATE_FAILED, TASK_STATE_CANCELED, TASK_STATE_REJECTED, and TASK_STATE_UNSPECIFIED.
claim: A2A v1.0 defines 9 task states including input-required and auth-required for human interaction workflows.

topic: A2A input-required state for clarification and data responses
query: A2A input-required task state human approval workflow
title: A2A Streaming and Async Tasks for Long-Running Agent Workflows - Rost Glukhov | Personal site and technical blog
snippet: A task in input-required pauses until the client sends additional message parts in the same contextId. For routine verification tasks—formatting checks, cross-referencing, or information retrieval—the state machine proceeds from submitted through working to completed, transiting the input-required state whenever an agent must pause for a clarification or data response from its counterpart.
claim: A2A input-required state pauses execution until client provides message parts in the same correlation context.

topic: MCP Elicitation protocol for human-in-the-loop interactions
query: MCP elicitation create protocol human in the loop agent
title: Enabling Human-in-the-Loop Workflows with MCP Elicitation | Glama
snippet: Elicitation allows MCP servers to pause tool execution and request structured input from the user. The server sends a JSON Schema describing what it needs, the client renders an appropriate form or prompt, the user responds, and execution resumes.
claim: MCP Elicitation enables servers to pause execution and request structured JSON Schema-described input from users.

snippet: AG-UI enables visibility, interruption, and approval during long-running agent tasks, with an event model covering text streaming, tool calls, state snapshots, and human interaction requests.
claim: AG-UI provides real-time visibility and interruption capability for long-running agents via event streaming model.

topic: Correlation context preservation in human-in-the-loop workflows
query: A2A input-required task state human approval workflow
title: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Protocol: The Future of Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems | HackerNoon
snippet: A workflow fails when the task reaches failed or rejected, or when a caller exceeds a timeout waiting for input that never arrives, so you should design explicit timeouts for human steps rather than letting approvals sit indefinitely.
claim: A2A workflows require explicit timeouts on human input steps to prevent indefinite waits during approval.
